Sam —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level proposal below; attaching an editable worksheet with numbers and a draft SOW language for milestone/crediting rules. Key points first:

- Tranches: 3-part split to minimize upfront capex: 30% at pilot start, 30% at KMS/HSM provisioning + successful audit smoke test, 40% at production cutover (30 days of SLA verification).
- Evidence: we propose three artifact classes: (A) Configuration proofs (screenshots, signed provisioning receipts), (B) Attestation artifacts (HSM attestation report or vendor cert + runbook checklists), (C) Functional audit logs (sample export + ingestion verification). Each artifact mapped to the tranche it unlocks.
- Sliding-scale credits: yes — if a milestone misses the target by >14 days we apply a 50% credit of that tranche back to monthly hosted usage invoices until remediation completes. This preserves momentum while addressing finance concerns.

I attached: 1) Implementation_Credit_Worksheet.xlsx (line-item mapping + timing), 2) MedHarbor_SOW_draft.pdf (milestone language + acceptance criteria).

I copied Laura (commercial/legal lead) and Aditya (solutions engineer) to help scope acceptance criteria precisely. If that approach works, we can convert language into SOW and DocuSign-ready addendum.

Next steps: propose a 30-minute call Thursday 9/9 to run through the worksheet and lock milestones.

Best,

Sam / Marcus —

Quick clarifying notes from legal/commercial on the acceptance language we typically use so it's clear to your auditors:

1) "Provisioning proof" = dated provisioning logs exported from Redwood's control plane + customer-signed checklist confirming keys/certs onboarded.
2) "HSM verification" = vendor attestation (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Confidential VM attestation or third-party HSM cert) OR Redwood-provided HSM self-check logs; must include a nonce challenge test (we can share a template).
3) "Audit log sample" = 7-day window export (gzip CSV) demonstrating retention pipeline, plus a checksum validation file; ingestion confirmation from MedHarbor's analytics team.

On credits: we prefer the sliding credit to be expressed as an invoice-level line credit tied to milestone ID with an auto-expiry if remediation completes within 60 days. That avoids running credits indefinitely.

Marcus — can you add the exact wording for the SOW addendum section titled "Milestone Acceptance & Credit Mechanism"? I'll review and provide redline.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
